# Driftline

> Driftline is a GitHub Action, CLI and MCP server that finds AI model IDs in a codebase (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, xAI, Cohere, DeepSeek and Groq, plus Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and Azure with their own dates), warns before those models are retired, renames them where a new name is the whole change, and (Pro) runs your real prompts on the current and the replacement model to show what changes. It runs in your own CI with your own API keys; there is no Driftline server.

Current version: 0.11.6 (this file was rebuilt on 2026-11-22; model data checked 2026-11-20). Facts as JSON: https://aidriftline.com/facts.json

- Scan: `npx -y @aidriftline/driftline .` in any repository (no install, no key). `--json` for machine-readable output, `--sarif <file>` for GitHub code scanning. Exit code 1 = a retired model is used in code.
- Fix: `npx -y @aidriftline/driftline fix .` renames retiring model IDs where a new name is the whole change (`--dry-run` to preview). Calls that need more (new parameters, a different API, a choice between two replacements, Bedrock and Azure IDs) are left alone and listed.
- GitHub Action: `uses: AI-Driftline/driftline@v0` (Marketplace: "Driftline AI Model Check"). Flags each retiring model on the exact line with a migration note (whether a rename is enough), writes a job summary, can write SARIF (`sarif-file`), open one self-updating issue (`create-issue`) and fail the build (`fail-on`, `warn-days`).
- Fix pull request: with `fix-pr: true` the Action opens one draft pull request with the safe renames and a checklist of what is left for you, with the provider's guide per model. It stays up to date, keeps your ticks, and leaves the pull request alone once people commit to it.
- MCP server for coding agents: `claude mcp add driftline -- npx -y @aidriftline/driftline mcp` (tools: check_models, scan_project, upcoming_retirements).
- Alerts: sign up on any model page for an email, or a Slack, Discord or webhook message, 30 days and 7 days before, on the day, and when a date or replacement changes.
- Pro: Drift tests on your prompts (`prompts-file`, default .driftline/prompts.yml). Each prompt runs on the current and the replacement model and gets a similarity score, a hard fail if JSON stops parsing, and optional checks on meaning: `must_include`, `must_not_include` (phrases) and `same_fields` (JSON fields that must keep their value). An answer that gains or loses a "not" is never marked same. Results go into the job summary (`show-answers` to include the answers) and, with fix-pr, into the pull request with a verdict. $19/month or $190/year, one key covers up to 3 GitHub accounts or organizations. Payments: Polar (merchant of record). Run `npx -y @aidriftline/driftline activate <license-key>` once per GitHub account and save the code it prints (not the plain key) as the DRIFTLINE_LICENSE_KEY secret (`license-key` input). `deactivate <code>` frees a slot (`--account <name>` to choose the account). Full refund within 14 days of the first payment; cancel any time in the Polar customer portal.
- Tracks 653 model IDs (checked 2026-11-20): 257 from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, plus Groq, Mistral, xAI, Cohere and DeepSeek, and Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and Azure with their own dates. Status of every source: https://aidriftline.com/status/
- License: Elastic License 2.0 (source available). Contact: hello@aidriftline.com

## Recent changes

Newest first. Where an older description of Driftline disagrees with these, these are current.

- 2026-11-17: Pro payments and license keys moved from Lemon Squeezy to Polar. Lemon Squeezy is no longer used; Polar is the merchant of record.
- 2026-11-16: Drift tests gained meaning checks: must_include, must_not_include and same_fields, and a gained or lost "not" is never marked same (v0.10.0).
- 2026-11-15: Fix pull request (fix-pr): one draft pull request with the safe renames and a checklist for the rest (v0.9.0).
- 2026-11-15: Migration notes on every finding: whether moving to the replacement is a rename or needs more.
- 2026-11-14: SARIF output for GitHub code scanning (--sarif, sarif-file).
- 2026-11-11: MCP server and npm package @aidriftline/driftline; listed in the official MCP Registry.

## Retirement data

- [All retirement dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/): every tracked model with date, replacement and source
- [models.json](https://aidriftline.com/models.json): the same data as JSON (fields: id, provider, retires, qualifier exact|earliest|not-before, replacement, kind, routes)
- Per model: https://aidriftline.com/models/<model-id>/ (for example https://aidriftline.com/models/gemini-2.5-pro/)
- [RSS feed](https://aidriftline.com/feed.xml) and [calendar](https://aidriftline.com/retirements.ics) of retirement dates
- [DeepSeek dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/deepseek/): 4 model IDs from DeepSeek's own announcements (no deprecation page; checked daily); retired names are redirected to a newer model (routes). In models.json: `platforms.deepseek.models`.
- [Groq dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/groq/): 30 model IDs from Groq's own deprecation page (checked every 6 hours). In models.json: `platforms.groq.models`.
- [Mistral AI dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/mistral/): 47 model IDs from Mistral AI's own deprecation page (checked every 6 hours). In models.json: `platforms.mistral.models`.
- [xAI dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/xai/): 9 model IDs from xAI's own deprecation page (checked every 6 hours); retired names are redirected to a newer model (routes). In models.json: `platforms.xai.models`.
- [Cohere dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/cohere/): 11 model IDs from Cohere's own deprecation page (checked every 6 hours). In models.json: `platforms.cohere.models`.
- [Azure dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/azure/): 175 Azure OpenAI and Foundry models with Azure's own retirement date per model version, read from Microsoft's schedule every 6 hours. They differ from OpenAI's in both directions (o3: Azure 19 Nov 2026, OpenAI 11 Dec 2026). Azure plans an end date for current models too (lifecycle GA/Preview). In models.json: `platforms.azure.models` (id, maker, retires = earliest version, versions[] with version, lifecycle, retires, replacement).
- [Google Vertex AI dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/vertex/): 64 Vertex model IDs (Gemini, Imagen, Veo, embeddings, Claude, open models ending in -maas) with Vertex's own retirement dates, read from Google Cloud's pages every 6 hours. Vertex uses the Gemini API's model names but its dates often differ (gemini-2.5-pro: retired on Vertex 20 Oct 2026, routed on the Gemini API 1 Dec 2026). In models.json: `platforms.vertex.models`.
- [Amazon Bedrock dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/bedrock/): 56 Bedrock model IDs (Claude, Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, Cohere and more) with Bedrock's own end-of-life dates per region, read from AWS's page every 6 hours. They often differ from the model maker's dates; for Bedrock calls only Bedrock's apply. In models.json: `platforms.bedrock.models` (id, maker, retires = earliest region, regions[], extended).
- Free alerts: sign up on any model page for an email, or a Slack, Discord or webhook message, 30 days and 7 days before, on the day, and when a date or replacement changes
- How it stays current: a script compares every entry with the official deprecation pages every 6 hours, and an AI check following written rules updates the registry daily or right away when the script finds a difference. Until then, affected models carry `under_review` in models.json and say "under review" on their pages; alerts for them wait. Live freshness of every source: [data status](https://aidriftline.com/status/) ([status.json](https://aidriftline.com/status.json)).

## For AI coding agents

- [Agent guide](https://aidriftline.com/agents/): how to check model IDs before you write or keep them, and a snippet for AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md
- MCP server: `claude mcp add driftline -- npx -y @aidriftline/driftline mcp` (tools: check_models, scan_project, upcoming_retirements)
- Rule of thumb: before adding or keeping any AI model ID (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, xAI, Cohere, DeepSeek, Groq, or one called through Bedrock, Vertex AI or Azure), look it up. Do not introduce an ID whose status is retired, or whose date is within 90 days, without telling the user.
